ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.label: storm tower
ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.leavesWhy: the readers take their mast, rods and tents home with them; what they keep of the colony is the record of its storms

texts.li: Two readers of {FACTION} and their apprentice are walking up {PLACE} with a glass mast in pieces and two rods, {X_nameDef} at the front. They will write down every storm that passes for a week.
[lowtech] Two readers of {FACTION} and their apprentice are walking up {PLACE} with a tall pole and a basket of glass jars. They will keep count of every storm for a week.

{X_nameDef} and another reader of {FACTION} have come up {PLACE} with their apprentice to set up a storm tower. The weather here has never been written down, {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef}, and they mean to watch it for a week.

[summer] Readers of {FACTION} are walking up {PLACE} in the heat with a mast in pieces on their backs. Summer storms come fast, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and they want every one of them written down.

settled.li: {FACTION}'s readers have pitched their tents {PLACE} and are setting up a glass mast and two rods beside their fire.
The readers have made camp {PLACE}, their mast of sealed glass going up between the tents.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Conclave says the colony's sky is worth a lifetime of watching, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay and keep its weather.
{X_nameDef} of the storm tower asks whether the colony would keep a reader of its own to watch its sky, rather than send {X_objective} back to the glass towers.

farewell.li: [left,taught] The readers took down their mast and rods and went, with {STORMS} storms written down. They left a sealed vial at the gate and the season's forecast, and the one of the colony who sat their night watch can read the glass now.

[left] The readers took down their mast and rods and went, with {STORMS} storms written down. They left a sealed vial at the gate and the season's forecast: the Conclave will watch the colony's sky for the season.
The readers took down their mast and rods and went back to the road.

lines.li: Never wrong, never sure.
The sky is the world thinking aloud.
Every storm is written down.
Check the vials before you sleep.
The glass is clear tonight.
[rain] Fill a vial, quickly, before it stops.
[morning] Read the glass before breakfast.
Write the hour, the wind and what followed.
[storm] Stay off the mast while it's like this.

momentLines.li: [mast] The mast is up, now the rods.
[storm] Note the hour it came in.
[strike] That one came down past the rods.
[watch] The glass is clouding, it will not be long.
[watch] Something is coming in, I can feel it in the glass.

helpTexts.li: [tales] {A_nameDef} sat with the readers by their fire and heard how a glassblower whose village lost its harvest to hail learned to read a frost in the glass a week before it came.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat with the readers while they sealed the day's vial and heard what is written on the brass caps on the oldest shelves.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} up to sit the night watch
li.tip: {A_nameDef}, the colony's best at the fields, goes up to the readers' mast for the evening and sits the watch with them, learning how they read the glass. When they go, {A_pronoun} can read it for a season.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is going up to the readers' mast to sit the watch with {X_nameDef}.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to see to the apprentice
li.tip: The colony's doctor goes over to the readers' camp and tends whoever of them is ill, with the colony's medicine where there is any.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is going over to the readers' camp to see to their apprentice.

ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.label: grove-keepers in the burn
ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.leavesWhy: the Mossborn leave nothing in a planting but the saplings

texts.li: Grove-keepers of {FACTION} are walking in {PLACE} with axes and bundles of saplings, {X_nameDef} at the front. They will clear the burn and replant it.
[lowtech] Grove-keepers of {FACTION} are walking in {PLACE} with stone axes and baskets of saplings. They will clear the burn and plant it again.

{X_nameDef} and the grove-keepers of {FACTION} have come to the burnt ground {PLACE} with saplings on their backs. What the fire took is owed back, {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef}, and they will clear the dead wood and plant again.

[spring] Grove-keepers of {FACTION} are walking in {PLACE} in the planting season, with saplings wrapped in wet moss. They will clear the burn and plant it, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, a seedling for every tree the fire took.

settled.li: The grove-keepers have made camp {PLACE} at the edge of the burn, their saplings heeled in by the fire.
{FACTION}'s grove-keepers have set up camp {PLACE}. While they are here they ask that the colony fell no tree within their planting.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Mossborn says the colony's land could use a keeper for its trees, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay and tend them.
{X_nameDef} of the grove-keepers says the colony's trees would do better with someone to keep the count, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay.

farewell.li: [planted,blight] {FACTION}'s grove-keepers packed up and went. They cut out the blighted plants and planted {PLANTED} saplings near the fields, and their ledger counts them as the colony's planting.

[planted,planter] {FACTION}'s grove-keepers packed up and went. They planted {PLANTED} saplings across the burn, some of them beside the colony's own planter, and their ledger counts them as the colony's planting.
[planted] {FACTION}'s grove-keepers packed up and went. They planted {PLANTED} saplings across the burn, and their ledger counts them as the colony's planting.
The grove-keepers packed up their camp and went back to the road.

lines.li: Every tree you fell owes the world a seedling.
The forest remembers every axe.
Ash is good ground for a young tree.
In the end we are all the grove.
Mind the roots when you walk.
[morning] Water the new ones first.
Clear the dead wood, but leave the stumps.
[rain] Good rain for planting.
One seedling for every tree the fire took.

momentLines.li: [cut] This one is only good for the fire now.
[felled] You cut within the planting, so we are going.
[fire] It has caught again, get the beaters.
[plant] Firm the soil around it, gently.

helpTexts.li: [tales] {A_nameDef} sat with the grove-keepers by their fire and heard how the first grove was planted, an acorn beside every stump in a valley the war had cut down.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat with the grove-keepers among the young trees and heard how the Mossborn bury their dead under saplings, so that each of them becomes part of the grove.

li.label: Send them food for the week (10 meals)
li.tip: One of the colony carries ten meals out to the grove-keepers' camp.

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Mossborn has come to the gate. Clearing the burn is hungry work, {X_pronoun} says, and asks whether the colony could spare some food for the week.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} says they will gather what they can from the woods.

outcomes.li: Ten meals are going out to the grove-keepers' camp.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to plant beside them
li.tip: {A_nameDef}, the colony's best at the fields, goes out to the burn and works beside the grove-keepers for a few hours, learning as they plant.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is going out to the burn to plant beside {X_nameDef}.

ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.label: Banner's company
ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.leavesWhy: a company on the march leaves nothing behind for whoever follows it

titles.li: The Banner camps at the edge

texts.li: A company of {FACTION} is marching in {PLACE} in step, {X_nameDef} at the front. They will camp a night or two on their way to a contract.
[lowtech] A war band of {FACTION} is walking in {PLACE} in a long file, spears on their shoulders. They will camp a night or two on their way.

Soldiers of {FACTION} are marching in {PLACE} in good order, {X_nameDef} calling the step. They are on their way to a contract, {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef}, and will camp a night or two before going on.
[winter] A company of {FACTION} on a winter march is coming in {PLACE}, {X_nameDef} at the front. They will camp a night or two to rest before the road to their contract.

settled.li: The Banner's company has its fire going {PLACE}, bedrolls laid out round it in rows and weapons stacked within reach.
{FACTION}'s company has made camp {PLACE}. A sentry walks the edge of it, and the rest are mending kit by the fire.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the company camped {PLACE}, came to the gate with {X_possessive} pack on. {X_pronoun} has marched far enough, {X_nameDef} says, and asks whether there is a place here; the Banner will hold it against the colony.
{X_nameDef} of the company says {X_possessive} contract is done and {X_pronoun} has no wish to sign another, and asks whether the colony would take in a soldier who wants to stop.

farewell.li: [caught] After the fight at the edge of the colony's land, the company carried its wounded out at dawn and marched on to its contract.
[enlisted] The company rolled its bedrolls at dawn, drilled once more and marched off, and one of the colony's own is on the road to join them for the season.
[brawl] The company rolled its bedrolls at dawn and marched off, the bet at the fire settled and not spoken of again.
The company rolled its bedrolls at dawn, drilled once more and marched off in step.

lines.li: Paid to the day, held to the day.
Every name on the Roll.
Keep your boots dry and your blade drier.
We march at first light.
No pay, no wall.
[morning] Fall in, we march at first light.
[evening] Boots off and feet up, we march early.
[rain] Keep your kit dry, it's a long march yet.
Count the rations, the paymaster will ask.

momentLines.li: [drill] Again, from the top, feet first.
[drill] Form up, and keep the line straight.
[bet] A day's pay says you cannot throw it farther than me.
[drill] Hold the line, and nobody breaks step.
[bet] Double or nothing, and the loser stands the night watch.

li.label: Have the sergeant drill {A_nameDef}
li.tip: {A_nameDef} spends a few hours at the company's fire being drilled by the sergeant. Practice in melee.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} has gone over to the company's fire, where {X_nameDef} is drilling {A_objective} with a practice blade, feet first.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} with the company for the season
li.tip: {A_nameDef} sets out for the Banner's nearest town to serve with the company for fifteen days, and comes home with a soldier's pay and what the drill ground taught. The roads there and back are the game's own.

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} has come up from the company's camp. The company is short of hands for this contract, {X_pronoun} says, and asks whether one of the colony's fighters would enlist for the season, for a soldier's pay.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} nods and goes back to the camp.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is packing for the road, to join the company at the Banner's town for the season.
